title: Vaughan condo shooting: Three victims were members of the condo board, gunman identified as 73-year-old resident
subtitle: Three men and two women were killed, York police said in a news conference on Monday afternoon. A sixth victim, a 66-year-old woman, was seriously injured and remains in hospital.
article: Six people are dead after a mass shooting at a Vaughan condo building Sunday , including the suspect, a man who died after an interaction with York Regional Police. Read the latest updates here.

6:02 p.m. Francesco Villi had a lengthy history of threatening members of the building's board and believed they had a conspiracy to "systematically murder" him, court documents and online posts indicate.

He was set to return to court Monday as the board sought to have a judge find him in contempt for violating a previous order to not contact the board, to stop threatening its members and building staff and to cease posting about them on social media.
The condominium wanted Villi gone - it sought a penalty from court to force him to sell and vacate his unit within 90 days, a factum filed in court by the condominium corporation last month said.
Villi never made it to court.
Read more on this story here.
6 p.m. Here's what we know, and don't know about the Vaughan condo shooter Francesco Villi. Read the story here.
3:39 p.m. John Di Nino confirmed to The Canadian Press his wife Doreen had been shot at the building on Sunday and was undergoing emergency surgery in hospital on Monday.
"It's so overwhelming right now," said Di Nino, who is a condo board member. "We're just hoping and praying."
Police said they were not yet able to release the identities of the five people killed.

2:45 p.m. Doreen Di Nino, wife of ATU Canada President John Di Nino, was identified as the injured victim in the shooting in a union message earlier on Monday. "I have been asked to provide comments after the terrible events yesterday in Vaughan," John Di Nino said in a statement to the Star. "This is obviously a very difficult time for my family, and I would ask that our privacy be respected. I intend to make no further comment at this time."

2: 24 p.m. Toronto Mayor John Tory tweeted his condolences. "On behalf of all Toronto residents, I extend condolences to our neighbours in the City of Vaughan in the wake of last night's horrific shootings, Tory said. Ontario Premier Doug Ford also tweeted that he is "shocked and saddened" by the shooting. "All of Ontario is thinking of the victims of this senseless violence and the family and friends grieving their loss. Thank you to our first responders for bravely being on scene," Ford said.

2:15 p.m When asked by a reporter about the gunman's relationship with the victims, York police said they can't report or confirm any information yet because police are still interviewing people and executing search warrants. "There's a lot of work still to be done. It's going to take several days to get through a lot of information," York police said.
Police would not provide age ranges for the victims.
York police said they received the call at 7:21 p.m. Sunday night and "within three minutes and 20 seconds or so our officers were on scene."

Police will continue to work with the coroner's office to find out when the post-mortem examinations will be completed, at which time they will be able to release more information on the shooting victims and provide support to the affected families.
2:08 p.m. York Regional Police have been notified that the coroner's office is working to identify the shooting victims and aren't permitted to release their names at this time.

Three men and two women were killed, said York police in a news conference on Monday afternoon. A sixth victim, a 66-year-old woman, was seriously injured and remains in hospital. York police say they are protecting her identity at this time
All victims live in the condo building, York police said, and confirmed that three of the victims were members of the condo board.
Multiple search warrants will be executed, said police, but until that time investigators "can't rule anything out."

2:04 p.m. The officer who shot suspect Francesco Villi is a 24-year veteran of the force, York Regional Police Chief Jim MacSween announced during a news conference Monday afternoon, adding the officer "likely saved lives by stopping Villi." Villi lived on the first floor, but was killed on the third floor.
12:48 p.m. Vaughan Mayor Steven Del Duca announced on Twitter that flags at city facilities have been lowered to half-mast in memory of the mass shooting victims.

12: 40 p.m. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau tweeted his condolences to the families and friends of the shooting victims. "I'm keeping you in my thoughts. To the person who was injured: I'm wishing you a fast and full recovery. And to the first responders: Thank you for your hard work and your professionalism."
12:13 p.m. Kristy Denette, a spokesperson for the SIU, spoke to reporters Monday afternoon.
The shooter had a semi-automatic handgun that was recovered at the scene, said Denette.
Officers located multiple deceased victims located on different floors, according to the SIU.

Police received initial calls for the shooting beginning at 7:20 p.m. and the gunman was pronounced dead shortly afterwards inside the building in a hallway after 8 p.m., Denette said, adding its unclear if the man was shot on the floor he lived on.
Denette believes there wasn't an exchange of gunfire between the armed gunman and police, but that it was shots fired from a single police officer that killed the gunman.

12 p.m. Current condo board member Tony Cutrone told the Star Monday morning that he became part of the board in part because his elderly mother - for whom he owns a unit - had been bullied by Villi in the past.
He said he was not there Sunday when the gunman opened fire in several condo units. Since the attack, he said he has tried and failed to contact other board members.
"I messaged and tried to call them and they didn't call back," he said, still reeling from the news.

After the shooting, officers "came in with rifles" to his mother's unit "looking for me making sure I was OK," he said. His mom then called him to ask what was going on, which is how he learned of the attack.
Read more: Man identified as Vaughan mass killer targeted condo board in 'frivolous and/or vexatious' lawsuit

(Updated) 11:40 a.m. In a statement Monday morning, Amalgamated Transit Union Local 113, the largest union representing TTC workers, said that the wife of the union's national president had been shot in the attack but survived. Local 113 said Doreen Di Nino, who is married to ATU Canada president John Di Nino, was undergoing emergency surgery Monday.
"We are grateful to learn that she has survived this horrific incident and is undergoing emergency surgery today," the union wrote.
The ATU later deleted their statement and clarified in an email to the Star that it was intended as a message for ATU Local 113 members.

11:34 a.m. The gunman who killed five in a mass shooting inside a Vaughan highrise before being himself shot dead by police late Sunday was a resident who had targeted the building's condo board in years of lawsuits, according to a source with first-hand knowledge of the "horrific" incident.
Resident Francesco Villi, 73, had been in a long-standing dispute with the members of the condo board before he opened fire Sunday, the source told the Star.
Read more: Man identified as Vaughan mass killer targeted condo board in 'frivolous and/or vexatious' lawsuit
11:29 a.m. The SIU is confirming that the shooter used a semi-automatic gun.
11:20 a.m. Tony Cutrone owns a unit for his elderly mother and was a member of the condo's board of directors.
He wasn't at the condo when the shooting happened.
"I messaged and tried to call them and they didn't call back," he told the Star on Monday, still reeling from the news.
11: 17 a.m. Vaughan mayor Steven Del Duca said he heard about the shooting yesterday evening around 8 p.m.

"I am absolutely shocked and heartbroken that five individuals have lost their lives...and for this to happen in a community like Vaugan...is devastating," said Del Duca, speaking in front of the crime scene Monday morning.
"It's just horrifying and i can't imagine what the victims families are going through right now."
Del Duca says despite a rash of violent incidents in recent months, he stressed the city is "very safe" has plans to address community concerns around safety in coming months.

11 a.m. A spokesperson for the SIU, Ontario's police watchdog, will be providing updates to the media live from the scene at noon, the agency announced on Twitter. Star reporters Noor Javed and May Warren will be at the scene.
10:57 a.m. About 15 police cars and a large forensic identification truck remained outside the highrise Monday morning. The main entrance to the building was taped off.
"It's just shocking to be honest," said Jordan Bennett, a building resident who went out to get food Sunday night and returned to find a heavy police presence at the building.
"I feel pretty safe here so I'm pretty shocked to hear something like this happened."
Speaking to reporters Monday morning, Vaughan Mayor Steven Del Duca called the shooting a "horrific act" and offered condolences to the victims' families.
"I know that we all sincerely hope for a speedy recovery for the individual who was wounded, who we believe is recovering," Del Duca said.
"And I want to thank all of our brave first responders for the work that they did yesterday to secure what I know must have been a very difficult situation."
Police said their investigation is active and ongoing, while the SIU said six investigators, including two in forensics, have been assigned to probe the police response.
10:37 a.m. John Santoro, who lives at Bellaria Residences, said he served on the condo board for about a year several years ago.

Speaking to reporters outside the building Monday, he said the situation was "tragic," and offered his condolences. On Sunday night, he "heard a commotion in the corridor" he said and "when I opened my door police were in the corridor," with "rifles right outside my door in theelevator lobby." A tactical unit then came in later around 10:30 to 11 p.m to clear the building.
10:17 a.m. A source close to the investigation into a shooting that killed five people at a Vaughan condo says the victims were found in different units in the building.
The source also says the suspected gunman, who was shot dead by police, lived in the building.
Ontario's police watchdog has said the gunman suspected in the Sunday night shooting at the Vaughan condo was a 73-year-old man.
Police had responded to reports of an active shooter around 7:20 p.m. Sunday and were met at the condo with a "horrendous scene," Chief Jim MacSween said in late-night news conference.
The Special Investigations Unit, which is probing the police response, said a York Regional Police officer shot the suspected gunman, who died at the scene.

10 a.m. York Regional Police Chief Jim MacSween will provide an update on the investigation into the shooting at Bellaria Residences in Vaughan at 2 p.m. Police say they are still working to identify the victims and notify families.

Monday: Early Monday morning, residents were allowed to re-enter the condo building near Vaughan Mills shopping mall. The condo was cordoned off by police officers, with two cars towed away by police Monday morning.

Sunday, 7 p.m.: Around 7:20 p.m. police were called to a building at 9235 Jane Street near Rutherford Road around 7:20 p.m. following a report of a male active shooter, said police spokesperson Const. Maniva Armstrong. Six people were reported dead, including the suspected gunman, a 73-year-old man. One other victim was taken to hospital. The building was evacuated while police conducted a search.

York Regional Police notified the SIU - which investigates in cases of death or serious injury involving police - who were on the scene while dozens of police cruisers lined the stretch of Jane Street in front of the building.
